passage:
Charu, promise you won't laugh. Me, Rekha, the sensible one, and I've been jealous of Ishaan's exes.

He mentioned a girl from school once, just once, and I couldn't stop. I asked what they used to do on Sundays, whether he'd loved her more than me, how long they had kept texting. He answered honestly at first, and then he got tired of it. And in our last argument, I actually said, "Well, you'd have gone to her party, wouldn't you?" like a weapon.

I saw his face fall. Later, on my own, I realised the questions weren't about her at all. I was scared I'd never be as interesting as anyone before me.

So I told him that: "It's my fear, not a charge against you." He looked so relieved. We haven't talked about her since, and I don't need to.

qa.q: Which sort of questions did Rekha ask Ishaan about the girl from school?
qa.a: Rekha asked what they used to do on Sundays, whether he had loved her more than Rekha, and how long they had kept texting.

qa.q: What did Rekha realise about those questions when she thought about them alone?
qa.a: Rekha realised they were not really about the ex at all, but about a fear of never being as interesting as anyone before.

qa.q: What went wrong with the way Rekha used the past in their argument, and what fixed it?
qa.a: Rekha used the ex as a weapon and hurt Ishaan, and it improved when Rekha named the fear as Rekha's own instead of making it a charge against him.

qa.q: How does Ishaan feel during the repeated questions?
qa.a: He answers honestly at first, then gets tired, so he probably feels interrogated and worn down.

grounding: Shows jealousy about a partner's exes, with the fear named and the past no longer used as a weapon.

passage: In a Sector 17 café in Chandigarh, Sumit's phone lit up with a message from Riddhi, his ex, congratulating him on his internship. Baljeet saw the name and felt the old knot tighten. She had already asked him, more than once, how long they'd dated, why they broke up, whether Riddhi was prettier. Last month, in an argument about something else entirely, she'd thrown it at him: 'Maybe you'd rather be with Riddhi.' She remembered his face then. Now she held her tea and made herself breathe. The past wasn't a threat; Sumit had chosen her every day for a year. 'Can I be honest about something?' she said. 'When her name comes up, I get scared I'm a replacement. It's not about anything you've done. And I'm sorry I used it in that fight.' Sumit reached across the table. 'You're not a replacement. Thank you for saying it like that instead of asking twenty questions.' The knot loosened.

qa.q: What did Riddhi congratulate Sumit on?
What was Baljeet afraid of when Riddhi's name came up?
qa.a: She was scared of being a replacement, a jealous fear rooted in the past.

qa.q: What did Baljeet do differently this time?
qa.a: She named the fear honestly, apologised for using it in a fight, and didn't interrogate him.

qa.q: How did Sumit respond to Baljeet's honesty?
qa.a: He reassured her she isn't a replacement and thanked her for sharing it without twenty questions.

grounding: Shows a young woman jealous of her partner's ex, accepting the past isn't a threat and talking about the fear instead of interrogating or using it as a weapon.

passage:
'You still have photos with him on your profile,' Saurabh said, trying to sound casual. 'From Goa. Three years ago.'
Madhuri looked up from her laptop. 'Rahul? Yeah. I never went back and deleted anything.'
'Why not? Do you still...'
He stopped. He could hear himself building up to twenty questions.
'Still what?'
Saurabh sat on the arm of the sofa. 'Sorry. Let me start again. When I saw those photos, I felt jealous. And scared. Like I'm competing with someone who isn't even here.'
'You're not competing with anyone. That was a different time, a different me.'
'I know. My brain doesn't always know it.'
'Do you want me to delete them?'
He thought about it. 'No. That's your history. I don't want you erasing it for me. I just wanted to tell you the fear instead of fighting about the photos.'
Madhuri smiled. 'That's the most grown-up thing you've said all month.'
'Don't get used to it.'

qa.q: Where were the old photos with Rahul taken?
What did Saurabh feel seeing the photos?
qa.a: He felt jealous and scared, as if competing with someone who wasn't even there.

qa.q: What did Saurabh do instead of interrogating Madhuri?
qa.a: He stopped himself mid-question and named his fear honestly, without asking her to erase her past.

qa.q: How does Madhuri see the photos?
qa.a: As a different time and a different version of herself, not a threat.

grounding: Shows a young man jealous of his partner's ex, stopping an interrogation and talking about the fear while accepting her past.
